claim_text: KEPCO says an outside cyber intrusion got into its systems and personal data was leaked
summary: KEPCO's own notices of Nov 22 say the leak was caused by a cyber intrusion: features offered for customer convenience became the target of an outside cyberattack, and it detected outside illegal access attempts on KEPCO ON on Nov 20.
detail: The KEPCO ON notice says it blocked the access attempts but found that some customers' data had been leaked in the process. Outlets add that KEPCO 'presumes' an outside attacker broke into both KEPCO ON and the SRM procurement system and took the data. The method and the attacker are not established.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own apology and KEPCO ON notice (Tier 1) state the cyber intrusion and the leak; outlets relay the same company statement. The privacy regulator's Nov 23 release (Tier 1) says KEPCO reported that a hacker leaked the data.

claim_text: About 1.52 million people's data was leaked across the two systems
summary: KEPCO says 650,487 KEPCO ON users and 869,761 SRM users were affected, which adds up to 1,520,248.
detail: KEPCO has not published a de-duplicated count: Chosunbiz and Electronic Times both say people may appear in both systems. Yonhap (Korean) says KEPCO ON has about 9.2 million users, so the leak there is about 7.1% of them.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The figures are KEPCO's, relayed by several outlets; the true number of distinct people is not given.

claim_text: KEPCO ON customers: IDs, bank accounts, card numbers and billing records leaked
summary: KEPCO's KEPCO ON notice lists the leaked items: customer number, name, resident or foreign registration number, phone, address, bank name, account number, account holder, card company, card number, cardholder, and bills.
detail: The notice says not every item was leaked for every person; customers can check their own case on the KEPCO ON site. Aju Press reports registration and card numbers were stored encrypted (see c012).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own notice (Tier 1) lists the items.

claim_text: Procurement system: names and IDs of company representatives, and staff contact details
summary: KEPCO's SRM notice says Nov 20 outside access leaked staff names, departments, employee numbers and work contacts, and suppliers' names, registration numbers, emails, addresses and phones. Outlets relaying KEPCO add staff mobiles.
detail: The notice gives no counts. Outlets relaying KEPCO say 426,827 company representatives and 442,934 KEPCO and company staff, 869,761 in all. Yonhap (Korean) says this is every SRM user, and that KEPCO is treating all of them as affected because it cannot pin down each person's exposure.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own SRM notice (Tier 1) lists the leaked items; the counts come from outlets relaying KEPCO.

claim_text: KEPCO learned of it on Nov 20, cut outside access and suspended the services
summary: KEPCO says it found outside illegal access attempts on Nov 20, blocked them, set up an emergency room, reported to the authorities, asked police to investigate and paused some outside services.
detail: KEPCO's apology says it has already asked police to investigate. Seoul Economic Daily gives KEPCO's timeline: it became aware at 6 AM on Nov 20 (Korea), reported to the climate ministry and the National Intelligence Service at 9:31 AM, and asked the Jeonnam provincial police to investigate at 12:31 PM the same day. That settles a difference between early reports: Yonhap (Korean) said it planned to, and Electronic Times said it had. The privacy regulator says KEPCO filed its report at about 6 PM on Nov 22 (Korea).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own apology and KEPCO ON notice (Tier 1) describe these steps.

claim_text: The National Intelligence Service and others are investigating the intrusion
summary: KEPCO says it is working with the National Intelligence Service, the climate and energy ministry and outside security experts to check for further leaks and the scope of harm.
detail: Outlets add that the ministry's cyber safety center is involved and that KEPCO will share details with government and financial authorities. No agency has published findings.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Stated in KEPCO's own apology (Tier 1); no agency statement found.

claim_text: How the attacker got in
summary: KEPCO has not said how the attacker got in. Its apology says some features offered for customer convenience and access became the target of an outside cyberattack, without naming them.
detail: KEPCO's line that attacks are getting more advanced, including with AI, is general, not a finding. Yonhap (Korean) quotes KEPCO saying the attacker appears to have pulled records one at a time and then stopped at some point, which is why only part of KEPCO ON's users were hit; KEPCO says the investigation will tell. We found no cause report. News1's report says the leak came to light through slow access and signs on the dark web; it does not name an entry route. Separately, KEPCO's own spring security review had found serious weaknesses (see c017); nothing public ties them to this breach. Financial News and the Kukmin Daily quote KEPCO saying it became a target as it expanded open digital services such as simplified authentication for checking and paying bills; that names an area, not a method. KEPCO's SRM notice says it blocked the illegal-access IP addresses and patched the related function, without saying what the function was. DailySecu (Nov 25) reports a tip that a flaw from a June bug-hunt pilot went unfixed; it found the reported flaws were patched and the breached part was a different system (c024).
label: Not established
why_it_supports: KEPCO's apology names a target area but no method; no cause has been published.

claim_text: Who is behind the attack
summary: KEPCO, the regulator and the outlets we read do not identify the attacker. The hacker emailed KEPCO (c019), posted on the dark web (c013) and spoke to KBS (c021); none of this identifies anyone.
detail: This page does not name or guess at an attacker.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing public names the attacker.

claim_text: A separate KEPCO breach in October affected 35,528 people
summary: KEPCO said on Oct 1 that about 24,000 staff's data was exposed on an outside webpage; by Oct 23 it was 35,528 with retirees and partner staff. Mostly names, affiliations and phones, plus coded face-recognition data of about 400 staff.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) and Aju Press report that KEPCO reported it to the privacy regulator and asked the Jeonnam provincial police to investigate. Both cite figures KEPCO gave a National Assembly committee member's office. KEPCO told a parliamentary audit on Oct 19 that the National Intelligence Service's regional branch alerted it on the afternoon of Oct 1 that staff data was exposed on a webpage hosted with a private cloud provider (Yonhap Oct 19, Today Korea); Segye Ilbo alone says the site was based in Hong Kong. Yonhap (Oct 4) says the page was not open to the general public, the data was removed about 32 hours after KEPCO noticed, and KEPCO said it was unrelated to AI-driven attacks on banks. Segye Ilbo (Oct 22) puts the later addition at 10,759 people: 10,691 retirees and 68 partner-company staff. The Leaves (Oct 20) and Today Korea (Oct 19) put the face-recognition records at 408 and say access details for 14,957 CCTV devices were also exposed; both relay the same KEPCO figures given to a lawmaker's office, and Today Korea adds that KEPCO has no record of how many times the page was viewed or downloaded.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Outlets relaying one set of company figures; the CCTV detail rests on KEPCO figures relayed by two outlets, and the Hong Kong detail on one outlet.

claim_text: Whether the Nov 22 breach is linked to the October one
summary: Yonhap (English) calls the October event a separate leak a month earlier. No source says whether the same attacker or the same weakness was involved.
detail: KEPCO says the cause is still being investigated. For the October leak, KEPCO told a parliamentary audit on Oct 19 that the intelligence service, the privacy regulator and the Jeonnam provincial police were looking at both a leak through a partner company and outside hacking (Yonhap Oct 19, Today Korea; The Leaves Oct 20 reports the same). Newspim (Nov 6) quoted KEPCO saying investigators' findings were due in mid-November. We found no published findings.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing published links or separates the two incidents.

claim_text: No follow-on harm found so far, KEPCO says
summary: KEPCO says no secondary harm has been found so far, and that it will ask government and financial authorities to watch for abnormal transactions on exposed bank and card numbers.
detail: It is early. KEPCO pledges remedies under the Personal Information Protection Act if customers are harmed. Seoul Economic Daily reports KEPCO is working with financial companies to prevent misuse and runs a round-the-clock call center. This claim is about what KEPCO has found, not proof that no misuse exists.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: KEPCO's own apology (Tier 1) states no secondary harm found so far.

claim_text: Registration and card numbers were stored encrypted, one outlet reports
summary: Aju Press reports that resident and foreign registration numbers and card numbers were stored in encrypted form.
detail: We did not find this in KEPCO's notices or in other outlets. Encryption at rest does not by itself mean the data cannot be read by an attacker.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relaying KEPCO; not in the company notices we read.

claim_text: A dark-web forum post on Nov 19 claimed to hold KEPCO user and bidding data
summary: DailySecu (Nov 20) and ZDNet Korea (Nov 21) report that a post on a dark-web forum dated Nov 19 claimed to hold KEPCO data: about 590,000 outside users' contact details, internal user records, supplier lists, and bid and contract records.
detail: Both outlets say the post did not name the system or route, and that whether the data really came from KEPCO's SRM was not confirmed. The post came one day before KEPCO says it became aware of the breach. Its figures do not match KEPCO's own counts. We did not visit the forum and do not name the poster. DailySecu's Nov 22 follow-up notes KEPCO's notices do not address the post or whether its data matches what was taken. The privacy regulator's Nov 23 release says KEPCO itself confirmed a dark-web posting on Nov 20 (see c019); it does not give the post's contents or figures. YTN (Nov 24) describes the same Nov 19 post as claiming about 49,000 internal user records, 592,000 outside user records and 950,000 supplier records, and military and government procurement files.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets report that the post exists; its contents are the poster's claim and are not verified.

claim_text: Bidding and contract records were also taken
summary: The forum post claimed about 400,000 bid-price records and 27,000 no-bid contract records; the hacker told KBS (Nov 23) this includes military and government facility bids. KEPCO told Seoul Shinmun contract data was not leaked.
detail: KEPCO's own notices list only personal data. Only the hacker supports the claim about bid and contract records; KBS reports it as the hacker's claim. KEPCO told KBS only that it is being investigated by the privacy regulator and is checking the facts. On Nov 24, KEPCO told Yonhap that bid information can be viewed without logging in and that the hacker's data seems to include already public material, though it is still checking. KEPCO told KBS (Nov 24) that it also checked an additional sample file obtained by the National Intelligence Service, and that the military and government facility bid information in it is already public on the Public Procurement Service's Nara Marketplace. That is KEPCO's account; the intelligence service has not commented.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: Only the poster claims it (repeated to KBS); KEPCO denies it, per one outlet.

claim_text: Power supply is not affected, the climate ministry says
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment said the breach is not currently affecting power operations, and that it will widen inspections to other state-owned energy companies.
detail: We did not find the ministry's own statement. The breached systems are a customer service platform and a procurement system, not grid control systems.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relaying the ministry.

claim_text: The KEPCO ON leak came to light through slow access, KEPCO says
summary: News1's Nov 22 report says the breach surfaced through access delays and dark-web indications. On Nov 24, KEPCO told Yonhap and YTN that it noticed the KEPCO ON leak when abnormal access overloaded its servers and slowed access on Nov 20.
detail: This matches KEPCO's account that it detected outside illegal access on Nov 20. The SRM procurement leak was found a different way: through the hacker's email and sample data (c019, c022). We could read News1's headline and subhead but not the full article text. This says how the breach was noticed, not how the attacker got in.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Outlets relaying KEPCO's own account of how it noticed the KEPCO ON leak; one company statement.

claim_text: KEPCO's own security review this spring found 218 'severe' weaknesses
summary: Money Today (Oct 19), citing KEPCO documents obtained by a lawmaker's office, reports KEPCO's April to July 2026 self-review rated 218 weaknesses severe: 197 on its servers, 21 in public-facing services.
detail: All 10 main public services tested had at least one severe weakness, mainly weak user authentication, weak access-rights checks and exposure of important data. KEPCO planned fixes through autumn; whether they were done is not public. Nothing public says any of these weaknesses was used in either breach.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relaying KEPCO's own audit documents.

claim_text: Korea's privacy regulator has opened an investigation
summary: The Personal Information Protection Commission said on Nov 23 that it received KEPCO's leak report and opened an investigation, forming an initial response team and carrying out an on-site inspection.
detail: The regulator says it will use on-site inspection and requests for documents to establish how the leak happened, how much harm it caused, and whether KEPCO met its duties under the Personal Information Protection Act to protect the data and to notify users and report the leak, and that it will act on any violations. It says it is monitoring with the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) to stop the leaked data spreading online, and it urges notified users to watch for suspicious verification requests, unknown links and app installs. It has published no findings yet.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The regulator's own press release (Tier 1); Yonhap and The Asia Business Daily report the same.

claim_text: KEPCO told the regulator it got an email from the hacker on Nov 19 and confirmed a dark-web posting on Nov 20
summary: The privacy regulator's Nov 23 release says KEPCO reported getting an email from the hacker about the data theft on Nov 19, and on Nov 20 confirming a dark-web posting and checking sample data from the hacker.
detail: Yonhap (Korean) reports the same sequence and adds that KEPCO then blocked outside IP access and suspended the services. This was not in KEPCO's own Nov 22 notices, which say only that it detected outside illegal access attempts on Nov 20. The regulator does not say what the email asked for, and no source we read mentions a ransom demand. We did not visit the dark web and do not name the hacker.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The regulator's own press release (Tier 1) gives this as KEPCO's account in its leak report; Yonhap reports the same.

claim_text: A sample from the hacker matched a real SRM user, KBS reports
summary: KBS (Nov 23) reports it got a sample of the data from the person behind the dark-web post, and a supplier staff member on the list confirmed by phone that they use KEPCO's SRM procurement system under the listed account.
detail: This is one outlet's own check of a small sample, not a check of the whole data set. KBS also spoke to an employee of a KEPCO power-generation subsidiary who said they had not yet been notified individually. We did not contact the hacker or anyone on the list, and we do not name the people KBS spoke to.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's independent check of a sample; not confirmed by KEPCO or investigators.

claim_text: The hacker says it is negotiating with KEPCO
summary: The hacker told KBS (Nov 23) that all of its data is genuine and that it is currently negotiating with KEPCO.
detail: KEPCO did not confirm any negotiation to KBS, saying only that it is being investigated by the privacy regulator and is checking the facts. On Nov 24, KEPCO told Yonhap the hacker has not tried to negotiate or asked for money, and that it has had no contact with the hacker since receiving the sample data (see c022). On Nov 24, KBS itself reported KEPCO's response to its earlier story: KEPCO says it has not negotiated with the hacker and was in touch only to get the sample. The two accounts conflict. This is the attacker's own claim, relayed by one outlet. We do not name the hacker.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: The attacker's own claim via one outlet; KEPCO denies any negotiation or demand, per Yonhap and KBS. Conflicting accounts.

claim_text: KEPCO says the hacker has made no money demand and has not tried to negotiate
summary: KEPCO told Yonhap and KBS (Nov 24) that the hacker has not tried to negotiate or demanded money, and that apart from getting a sample to check the data, it has had no contact with the hacker.
detail: KEPCO says it asked the hacker for sample data to check the claim, and from that sample found its SRM procurement system had been hacked. It says it could not pin down exactly whose data was taken, so it is treating all 869,761 SRM users as affected. This contradicts the hacker's claim to KBS that it is negotiating with KEPCO (c021). It is KEPCO's account; no investigator has commented. KBS (Nov 24) reports KEPCO's account that it got the hacker's email on Nov 19, received a sample file to check it, and confirmed the leak at 2:57 PM on Nov 20 (Korea); it says it has had no further contact or negotiation since and no money was asked for. KBS and YTN carry the same company account, so this still rests on KEPCO's word.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Yonhap, KBS and YTN relay the same KEPCO statement; outlets relaying one company statement count as one source.

claim_text: A dark-web listing offers about 26.5 million KEPCO data records for sale
summary: Women Economy Daily (Nov 24), citing an overseas threat-intelligence outlet, reports a dark-web sale listing with KEPCO's name offering about 26.5 million data records, with a public sample of 212 records.
detail: The outlet says the sample includes customer numbers, names, contact details, addresses, supply contracts, monthly power use, bills and unpaid counts. It notes that 26.5 million is a count of records, not people, and that one customer can have many monthly records; KEPCO's own count is about 1.52 million people. The listing is the seller's claim; neither KEPCO nor investigators have commented on it. We did not visit the dark web and do not name the seller.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: One outlet relaying a threat-intelligence report of a seller's listing; not checked by KEPCO or investigators.

claim_text: A tip says a weakness reported in a June government bug-hunt pilot was left unfixed and led to the leak
summary: DailySecu (Nov 25) got a tip that a KEPCO ON flaw reported in a June government bug-hunt pilot was not fixed. It found the pilot covered the KEPCO ON website, all reported flaws were patched, and the breached part is a different system.
detail: The pilot ran from June 29 to July 24, 2026, with the government, the National Intelligence Service and KISA; the flaws reported to KEPCO included possible data exposure and privilege escalation. DailySecu says nothing so far shows a pilot flaw caused this breach, and it could not learn when each fix reached KEPCO's live servers. The Personal Information Protection Commission is still investigating how the leak happened. This is about a possible cause, not a finding.
label: Unverified
why_it_supports: One outlet reporting an anonymous tip and its own check of it; no investigator has commented.
